newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Lufthansa off to strong start in 97.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Lufthansa off to strong start in 97.

text.p: Lufthansa AG said on Thursday it would end the first half of 1997 with profits higher than in the 1995 and 1996 periods due to strong passenger growth and cost-cutting at the German airline.
Lufthansa said the six-month performance prompted it to predict it could top the record 1995 results for the full year, provided industry conditions did not change.
"In the absence of major changes in the market, we expect 1997 results to be above the best-ever results in 1995," Lufthansa Chairman Juergen Weber said at the airline's annual shareholder meeting.
Lufthansa's first-half results, to be released on August 26, will top results from the same periods in 1995 and 1996 and even exceeded the airline's expectations, Weber said.
"We will end the first half of this year with profits significantly higher than the prior-year level and also above the good half-year results in 1995," Weber added.

Shareholders at the meeting were also set to vote on measures tied to the Bonn government's plans to sell off its remaining 36 percent stake in the airline and efforts to ensure that a majority of Lufthansa remains in the hands of Germans.
The measures, which include giving Lufthansa the right to buy shares if the percentage of foreign ownership rises above 40 percent, were expected to be given shareholder approval.
Lufthansa, which has only one major German shareholder with a 10 percent stake, must remain in majority control by Germans to guarantee the country's bilateral flight agreements.

The German government, which transferred its shares to the Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau (KfW) for 2.1 billion marks ($1.2 billion) in December 1996, intends to sell the shares in the autumn. No decision has been made on how the shares will be sold.

Lufthansa had hoped to post record earnings in 1996 when it reported a profit from ordinary activities of 686 million marks on sales of 20.8 billion marks. In 1995, Lufthansa reported a profit from ordinary activities of 756 million marks on sales of 19.9 billion marks.

But Lufthansa's hopes were dashed by higher fuel and operating costs, which Weber said rose eight percent to 22.2 billion marks. He noted that oil prices were not expected to rise during the rest of 1997.

In addition to cost-cutting measures aimed at slashing 1.5 billion marks, or 20 percent, off Lufthansa's operating costs in the coming years, Weber said the airline's "Star Alliance" partnership contributed 200 million marks to 1996 profits.
Lufthansa offers code-share flights and global marketing efforts with airlines that include United Airlines, Thai Airways International, Air Canada and Scandinavian Airlines System.
"The barometer is presently rising. Our passenger numbers are growing strongly, especially in the North Atlantic, Asian and Pacific markets," Weber said.

Passenger traffic on South American routes has recently been up about nine percent, while North American traffic has been up 8.5 percent. But Weber said the German market has failed to show much improvement.
"Demand so far this year has been lively," he said of flights to North and South America. "It has never been so good."

Lufthansa also said it was hopeful for a profit in its cargo unit in 1997 based on results from the first four months of the year but Weber said the fourth quarter would be a decisive factor influencing full-year results.

"The trend at the moment is positive," Weber said of the cargo unit, which reported a loss on ordinary activities of 59.8 million marks in 1996 despite a three percent rise in sales to 3.43 billion marks.
